overall: Atlanta is sitting at a running max of 84.2°F as of early afternoon, with temperature momentum having stalled completely (velocity = 0.0°F/hr). The morning showed a solid warming ramp from 73.4°F at 7 AM to 84.2°F by 1 PM, but the plateau in the last hour is notable heading into what should still be the peak heating window (roughly 2–4 PM ET). The relatively low dewpoint of 57.2°F means humidity is not a limiting factor for further warming, but the stalled velocity is a cautionary signal.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is exceptionally wide today: NBM (83.3°F) has already been busted by the current running max of 84.2°F, ECMWF (84.7°F) is nearly busted as well, while GFS (90.3°F) is a significant outlier suggesting ~6°F of additional warming — a scenario the ensemble signals sharply discount, with the 90–91°F tier registering only 5% probability and the 87–88°F tier at just 19%, both flagged Tier 4 (Avoid).
max_temp_prediction: With peak heating hours (2–4 PM) still ahead but momentum having stalled to zero at 1:05 PM, the most likely outcome is a modest additional gain of 1–2°F above the current running max. GFS's 90°F target appears unreliable given observed stalling and low ensemble support; ECMWF and NBM have effectively already been met or exceeded. The predicted daily high clusters near 85–86°F, with moderate confidence, contingent on whether solar heating can briefly re-accelerate temperatures before the afternoon cooling trend sets in.
